title: Adic finiteness for a projective-space projection
statement: Fix a prime l. For a scheme V let Qbar_l,V be the sheaf of locally finite continuous functions to an algebraic closure of Q_l: locally on V the values lie in a finite extension of Q_l. Let AdicSheaf_l(V) be the abelian category of modules over this sheaf, and call such a sheaf constructible if Zariski locally it admits a finite partition by locally closed constructible subschemes on which it is pro-etale locally finite free. These are the concrete sheaf models of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension] and [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]. Write D^b_c(V) for the objects of the ordinary derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] which are bounded for its standard t-structure and have constructible cohomology. Let l be a prime and K an algebraically closed field with char K != l. Let W be affine and t:W -> Spec K locally of finite type [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Let n be any finite type (possibly empty) and let p:P(Option n; W) -> W be relative projective space [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change], of fibre dimension the cardinality of n. For a constructible adic sheaf F on this projective space, Rp_*(F[0]) belongs to D^b_c(W).

source.place: Lemma 6.7.2, Proposition 6.8.11, Proposition 6.8.14 and Remark 6.8.15; affine compactification proof of sk-prop-sf-finiteness (SGA 4½, Theoreme de finitude, Theorem 1.1).

proof.text: The projection is proper and finitely presented by [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper]. Both base and source are noetherian and of finite type over K. As in Proposition 6.8.14, descend F[0] to a finite extension E/Q_l and choose a constructible integral lattice complex C over O_E; the existence argument is [lem-weil-pbc-lisse-e-constructible-integral-lattice] and Lemma 6.8.13. The lattice need not be lisse globally.

For each n >= 1 the derived reduction of C modulo pi^n is a bounded constructible finite-torsion complex. Classical proper finiteness [lem-fin-proper-bounded-constructible] makes its direct image constructible. Proper base change and the torsion cohomological-dimension bound for the projective-space fibres give a single bound for all n. The perfect two-term resolutions of O_E/pi^n give uniform bounds for the source reductions as well.

Apply the complete direct-image and perfect-reduction comparisons of Lemmas 6.5.9 and 6.5.11. The finite-level constructibility and uniform bounds give integral constructibility by Lemma 6.7.2, the proper case of [lem-sf-integral-direct-image-constructible].

Finally apply Proposition 6.8.11 to get bounded constructible cohomology, and Proposition 6.8.14 and Remark 6.8.15 to identify rationalization and passage to the locally finite Qbar_l coefficient sheaf with the ordinary ambient derived direct image on AdicSheaf_l. This is valid also for n empty (P^0_W) and for an empty base. Formalizing these coefficient comparisons remains necessary.

    (hK : ringChar K ≠ l) {W : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine W]
    (t : W ⟶ Spec (.of K)) [LocallyOfFiniteType t] (n : Type u) [Finite n]
    (F : AdicSheaf l ℙ(Option n; W)) (hF : IsAdicConstructibleSheaf F) :
    (_root_.DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.bounded ⊓
      _root_.DerivedCategory.homologyProperty (adicConstructibleSheaf l W))
      ((ℙ(Option n; W) ↘ W)_*ᵃ[l].rightDerivedFunctor.obj
        ((_root_.DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj F))
